title: Finite-size scaling of spin-wave scattering and enhancement in magnonic Fabry-Pérot nanoresonators
abstract: Magnonic neural networks require compact resonant nodes that scatter spin waves efficiently, concentrate spin-wave energy and can be reconfigured. Hybrid magnonic Fabry-Pérot resonators, formed by a ferromagnetic-metal stripe dipolar-coupled to a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) film, provide low-loss and programmable control of spin-wave transmission, but have so far been studied only for stripes that are long compared with the spin-wave wavelength. Here we use micromagnetic simulations to determine how the response of a 200-nm-wide CoFeB stripe on a 55-nm-thick YIG film evolves as the stripe length is reduced from infinity to 640 nm. An infinitely long stripe acts as a one-dimensional cavity that opens a transmission gap at the first-order resonance (1.70 GHz and 1.47 GHz for the parallel and antiparallel magnetic configuration) and enhances the out-of-plane precession amplitude in the YIG film by factors of about 5 and 12, without distorting the transmitted wavefront. For lengths of a few micrometers, backward-volume spin waves emitted from the stripe ends modulate the precession along the stripe and fragment the reflected and transmitted wavefronts. Below about 1.2 micrometer, the resonator scatters incident spin waves over the entire isofrequency contour of the film, with caustic beams that are most pronounced in the antiparallel configuration. In this regime the parallel configuration supports weakly enhanced quantized modes, whereas the antiparallel configuration supports a single mode with an out-of-plane enhancement of about 15. The width, thickness and shape of the stripe tune this mode by 50-100 MHz, and its strong enhancement lowers the onset of nonlinear frequency shift and fold-over to incident amplitudes of a few percent of the saturation magnetization. Sub-micrometer magnonic resonators are therefore promising reconfigurable nonlinear nodes for magnonic networks.
summary: This work simulates the size-dependent physics of magnonic Fabry-Pérot resonators, showing how reducing the stripe length fundamentally changes the spin-wave response. The key finding is that sub-micrometer resonators, particularly in the antiparallel magnetic state, support a single, strongly enhanced mode that can be tuned for use in reconfigurable nonlinear nodes for magnonic neural networks.
main_problem: The study investigates how the spin-wave scattering and energy enhancement properties of magnonic Fabry-Pérot nanoresonators change as the physical length of the ferromagnetic stripe is reduced from an infinite limit.
main_result: Below a critical length of approximately 1.2 $\mu$m, the resonator exhibits a strong divergence in behavior between parallel and antiparallel magnetic configurations, supporting a single, highly enhanced mode in the AP state.
method: The research relies on performing detailed micromagnetic simulations to model the spin-wave dynamics within the coupled YIG/CoFeB structure.
model_or_system: The system is a hybrid magnonic Fabry-Pérot resonator consisting of a CoFeB stripe dipolar-coupled to a YIG film. The simulations track spin-wave transmission, precession amplitude, and scattering behavior as a function of stripe length and magnetic configuration.
key_observables: Spin-wave transmission gaps, out-of-plane precession amplitude enhancement factors, and the evolution of quantized resonance modes.
important_parameters: Stripe length ($L$) varying from $\infty$ down to 640 nm; magnetic configurations (Parallel vs. Antiparallel); stripe width (200 nm) and YIG thickness (55 nm).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the difference in behavior between P and AP configurations is governed by the static stray field of the stripe ends, which dictates mode confinement.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of spin-wave amplitude and resonance features across different stripe lengths, comparing the ideal 1D cavity behavior to the complex scattering patterns observed in sub-micrometer structures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the ideal 1D cavity limit ($L=\infty$), then analyzing the transition through few-$\mu$m lengths where end effects (BV waves) appear, culminating in the distinct, highly enhanced single-mode behavior observed below $1.2 \mu$m.
why_interesting: The strong, tunable, and highly enhanced nonlinear response achieved in the sub-micrometer AP state makes this structure a promising candidate for implementing complex logic gates or memory elements in solid-state magnonic circuits.
